original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

scope_change_reason: Take Nick Petalas PR6428 open question 1. Narrow measured acceleration to a path-safe unique-blob candidate prefilter, a scoped preservation proof and controlled-history full-report/CLI conformance. Same-fixture timings are evidence, not a speed claim; no canonical historical replay is claimed.
actual_scope: An opt-in source-bound unique-blob digest prefilter preserving the original pinned-edit scanner per-path text/binary decisions and complete controlled-history reports.
bottleneck_link: Avoid transferring repeated nonmatching tree blobs into the raw candidate search without discarding Git path-policy checks; exact work accounting and no measured speedup claim.
stop_rule: Freeze science by 2026-11-02T23:37:21Z and reserve at least 15 minutes for verification and handoff. Stop on a concrete counterexample or after controlled report conformance; do not extend into a full canonical-history benchmark.
evidence: PROOF.md, authenticated SOURCE-PINS.json, primary RESULT.json and independently sealed ORACLE.json; VALIDATION.md records actual checks and limits.
author: ToikY
ai_assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the implementation, fixtures, proof and metadata; separate Codex agents supplied an independently sealed oracle and static review. This is AI corroboration, not independent human review.

nearest_work: PR6428 unchanged-head read reuse and explicit digest-search handoff
overlap.delta: Raw unique-OID candidate search with all alias expansion, original Git classification, controlled complete report/CLI equivalence and path-policy counterexamples.
overlap.limits: Sparse local notes, open PR body snapshots and visible Discussion claims do not cover all historical diffs, hidden replies or unpublished work.

open_questions.question: Does the opt-in candidate prefilter improve end-to-end runtime on PR6428 exact canonical 154-row historical fixture?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The extra unique-blob pass and final candidate grep may cost more than the original search; exact transfer counts alone do not establish speedup.
open_questions.first_step: Freeze the same base/head and complete Git-object closure used by PR6428; compare every report row and CLI result before repeating timing trials, including cold/warm context.
open_questions.blocked_by: Not run in this bounded session; requires an independently budgeted full historical object closure and benchmark.

open_questions.question: What explicit safe eligibility extension covers a caller enabling submodule recursion?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Superproject tree blobs cannot account for recursive submodule results.
open_questions.first_step: Specify submodule object/worktree/config and path-binding semantics before attempting an extension.
open_questions.blocked_by: Current adapter deliberately falls back for any gitlink or enabled/unsupported recursive configuration.
